propositions: Cloud's three whole-project readers (get_parent_map, get_comment_map, get_issuelinks_map) paginate opaque cursors via nextPageToken but have zero test coverage beyond single-page pagination (only 'isLast': True payloads tested)

The same pagination defect class (advance-by-requested-size, break-on-short-page) shipped three times on DC and was fixed only in production; Cloud's readers use opaque cursors (structurally immune to that bug) but lack regression nets

A test suite was added covering 250 items across three pages with assertions on cursor advance, both stop conditions (isLast and absent/null nextPageToken) in isolation, short-page handling, and structural AST guard to prevent unpaginated whole-project readers from being added silently

A real defect was discovered and filed separately: repeated cursor tokens cause infinite loops in these three readers because they lack the same-token-twice guard that fetcher._iter_pages has, making silent truncation invisible to fail-open exception handlers

Test mutations confirmed every oracle has teeth: breaking pagination after page one fails multiple tests; transplanting the DC short-page bug is caught only by a dedicated short-page variant; dropping either stop condition separately fails only its dedicated oracle
